title: Prolonged Grief Disorder in General Practice – State of Knowledge on the New Diagnosis and Dealing with Those Affected
summary:
Many bereaved people grieve when someone close to them dies. For most, the intensity of the grief eases over time. For some, however, the grief persists for a very long time and interferes with daily life - for example through great longing, emotional pain, sleep problems or the feeling that they can no longer cope with everyday life. This persistent form of grief has recently been officially recognized as a mental illness in its own right.
GPs are often the first port of call when it comes to treating and supporting grieving people. However, studies from abroad show that many doctors do not feel well prepared to care for people with prolonged grief. In some cases, there is a lack of knowledge about the symptoms, risk factors and treatment options. To date, there have been hardly any scientific studies on this topic in Germany.
The aim of this study is to find out what general practitioners in Germany know about prolonged grief and what experiences they have had in treating grieving patients. It also aims to find out how open they are to further training on this topic and what ideas and wishes they have for possible further training. In addition, those affected will be asked how they experience support from their GP practice, what they need, and what factors may influence their satisfaction with their GP.

interventions.name: Sub-study 1: General practitioners are questioned once using a questionnaire developed specifically for this study. Sub-study 2: In-depth semi-structured telephone interviews will be conducted with general practitioners. Topics will be their experiences with bereaved patients, attitudes and knowledge regarding the new PGD-diagnosis, as well as wishes, suggestions, and ideas regarding new training on PGD.

Sub-study 3: Focus group discussions will be conducted with bereaved patients to find out about their experiences with treatment from their general practitioners as well as their needs and wishes regarding treatment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Sub study 1: Specialists in outpatient GP care in zip code: 04 (Leipzig), sufficient knowledge of the German language and informed consent
Sub study 2: Specialists in outpatient GP care in Germany, sufficient knowledge of the German language and informed consent
Sub study 3 and 4: Loss of a close person within the last 3 years, visit to the GP practice due to complaints caused by grief lasting at least 6 months, sufficient knowledge of the German language and informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
None
